html:
Rabindranath Tagore was a Bengali poet, songwriter, novelist, painter and teacher, born in Calcutta in 1861. In 1913 he became the first person from outside Europe to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.

He was the youngest son of Debendranath Tagore, a leader of the Brahmo Samaj, in a family at the heart of the Bengal Renaissance. He wrote thousands of poems and more than two thousand songs, plus novels, short stories and plays, and took up painting in his sixties. The prize came after his own English versions of Gitanjali, "song offerings", found readers in London.

His songs are anthems of two nations: Jana Gana Mana in India and Amar Shonar Bangla in Bangladesh.

He founded a school at Santiniketan that grew into Visva Bharati University, where learning was meant to happen in the open air and across cultures. He gave back his British knighthood after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 1919. He admired Gandhi, and is often said to have first called him Mahatma, but he argued with him about narrow nationalism. He died in 1941.
